program_name: Architecture & Heritage (ARCHER) — Italian official name: Corso di Laurea Magistrale in 'Architettura e patrimonio / Architecture and Heritage'. Two-year Master of Science (laurea magistrale biennale), 120 CFU/ECTS over 4 semesters, comprising 6 exams (3 per year, of which 4 are large multidisciplinary integrated design laboratories) plus a compulsory external internship, 10 CFU of student-chosen elective activities and the final exam. Federico II internal course code: DB2 (the course carried the code P53 up to a.y. 2024/25; the 2025/26 Didactic Regulations are issued under DB2). Activation year on the official course record: 2020. Degree Programme Director / Coordinator: Prof. Andrea Pane (andrea.pane@unina.it, +39 081 2538061), who is also the designated contact person for international students. Run by the Department of Architecture (DiARC — Dipartimento di Architettura), within the Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School (Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base). Dedicated programme website: https://www.diarc.archer.unina.it/ . The course is explicitly designed to train an architect under Directives 85/384/EEC and EC 2005/36 with specialised competences in built heritage (design, restoration, conservation, maintenance and management of architectural, urban and territorial heritage), which is what distinguishes it from the traditional LM-4 paths.
level: master (second-cycle) — Italian 'laurea magistrale' of two-year duration (biennale), 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 CFU-ECTS. The orientamento.unina.it portal classifies it under 'Master's Degree'; the official course record at corsi.unina.it lists 'Course type: Laurea Magistrale, Duration: 2 anni'. This is NOT a single-cycle (a ciclo unico) architecture degree — it is the two-year graduate degree entered after a three-year bachelor, and it is therefore governed by the ordinary master's-degree rules rather than by the national architect-training admission competition.
teaching_language: English — the programme is delivered entirely in English. The official course record at corsi.unina.it/DB2 states 'Language: English'; the Didactic Regulations SUA-CdS general information block states 'Teaching language English'; orientamento.unina.it shows 'Language: ENG'. All taught units in the study plan (the four design studios, the integrated course of critical knowledge of heritage, and the integrated heritage management course) are marked 'Inglese' in the regulations; only the 'Ulteriori attività formative' (further training activities) line is marked 'Italiano/Inglese', because that slot is explicitly used to teach Italian to foreign students and other languages to Italian students. The final thesis is written in English (another language may be accepted on motivated request, but the presentation and discussion are in English in any case) and must contain an abstract in Italian. IMPORTANT NUANCE: despite being fully English-taught, the programme's entry requirements ALSO ask for 'a minimum level of knowledge of the Italian language'. This is not a B2 requirement — it is assessed during the admission interview and, where the level is insufficient, the student is directed to include Italian-language learning activities in their study plan (supported by the University Language Centre and by the elective-activities credits). The University's international pages separately confirm that for degree courses taught in ENGLISH 'level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required' for pre-enrolment and visa purposes.
campus: Naples historic city centre — Department of Architecture (DiARC), Complesso dello Spirito Santo, with entrances at via Toledo 402 and via Forno Vecchio 36, 80134 Napoli, Italy. The ARCHER 'Venue details' page states that all applied and teaching activities take place in the Spirito Santo complex; the orientamento page confirms 'All the classes are held in the complex of "Spirito Santo" that is the main building of the Department of Architecture, with access from via Toledo 402 and from via Fornovecchio 36.' A second DiARC building, Palazzo Orsini di Gravina (a Renaissance palace that has been the seat of the Faculty of Architecture since 1936), houses the Roberto Pane Library and the Area Architettura Library and hosts the final degree (graduation) sessions. The official course record at corsi.unina.it/DB2 gives the location simply as 'NAPOLI'. NOTE FOR CLARITY: this is NOT the Monte Sant'Angelo, Policlinico, Portici, San Giovanni a Teduccio or Frullone campus — it is the downtown architecture campus. Public transport: Metro Line 1 (Dante and Toledo stations), Metro Line 2 (Montesanto), Metro Line 5 / Circumflegrea, Metro Line 8 / Cumana, and the Montesanto–Vomero funicular. Student Administration Office: Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Architettura, segrearch@unina.it (https://www.unina.it/-/769229-segreteria-studenti-area-didattica-architettura). Department contact: infodiarc@unina.it; programme-specific address used in the ARCHER booklet for applicants: infodiarcarcher@unina.it.
degree_class: LM-4 — Architettura e ingegneria edile-architettura (Architecture and Building Engineering–Architecture). The official course record at corsi.unina.it/DB2 shows the class as 'LM-4 R - Architettura e ingegneria edile-architettura', where the 'R' suffix is the reformed ministerial class code applied from the 2025/26 re-accreditation; orientamento.unina.it and the Didactic Regulations both write it plainly as 'LM-4'. Federico II internal course code: DB2 (previously P53 — the ARCHER site publishes 'Didactic Regulations 2025/26 (DB2)' and 'Didactic Regulations 2024/25 (P53)', confirming the code change). Because the degree sits in class LM-4, graduates may sit the Italian State Examination for entry to the Register of Architects, Planners, Landscape Architects and Conservators (Albo degli Architetti Pianificatori Paesaggisti Conservatori) and enjoy professional recognition across the European Union.
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (Italian: 'accesso libero') with compulsory verification of curricular requirements and of the candidate's personal preparation. There is no ranked competition, no numerus clausus and no written admission test for this programme. Evidence: (a) orientamento.unina.it lists 'Admission: Libero' in the course fact box and states 'The access to the ARCHER course is free and therefore it is only subject to verification of the minimum prerequisites for access and personal preparation'; (b) Art. 5 of the 2025/26 Didactic Regulations states 'The Degree Program does not include local access programming' and 'Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it'; (c) CRITICALLY, ARCHER is NOT covered by the national restricted-access competition for architect-training courses under Law 264/1999. Federico II's 2026/27 architect competition, Decreto Rettorale DR/2026/2379 of 18/06/2026, lists in Article 1 exactly three courses — the single-cycle LM-4 'Architettura' (250 + 3 seats), the single-cycle LM-4 'Ingegneria edile-architettura' (90 + 2 seats) and the L-17 bachelor 'Scienze dell'Architettura' (176 + 4 seats). The two-year LM-4 ARCHER does not appear in that decree and therefore has no seat cap and no national test. HOWEVER, in practice a selective departmental pre-admission procedure applies to non-EU applicants resident abroad: they must submit a documentary dossier (including a portfolio and a recommendation letter) to the department, are likely to be called for an interview, and only then receive a 'pre-admission letter' which they attach to their Universitaly application. So the effective admission route is: (1) open access for Italian/EU candidates and non-EU candidates legally resident in Italy or in an EU country, subject to curricular-requirement and personal-preparation checks; (2) document screening + interview + pre-admission letter + Universitaly pre-enrolment for non-EU candidates resident abroad.
academic_requirements:
Set out in Art. 4 of the 2025/26 Didactic Regulations (source: SUA-CdS framework A3.a - RAD). The entry requirements are:
(1) DEGREE: possession of a degree in class L-17 – Scienze dell'Architettura (Sciences of Architecture), or in the old class 4 under Ministerial Decree 509/1999; OR possession of any three-year university degree or diploma (DM 270/04, art. 6) or a qualification obtained abroad in which the essential training activities of the L-17 curriculum have been completed. The ARCHER application-rules page phrases this simply as "Bachelor's Degree in Architectural Sciences (class L-17) or equivalent".
(2) MANDATORY CURRICULAR CREDIT TABLE (compliant with Directive 85/384/EEC). The candidate's prior degree must contain the following CFU/ECTS by disciplinary sector (SSD):
  • Mathematical disciplines for architecture — 8 CFU (INF/01 Computer science; ING-INF/05 Information processing systems; MAT/03 Geometry; MAT/05 Mathematical analysis; MAT/06 Probability and mathematical statistics; MAT/07 Mathematical physics; MAT/08 Numerical analysis; MAT/09 Operational research)
  • Physical-technical and plant engineering disciplines for architecture — 8 CFU (FIS/01 Experimental physics; ING-IND/10 Industrial technical physics; ING-IND/11 Environmental technical physics)
  • Historical disciplines for architecture — 16 CFU (ICAR/18 History of architecture)
  • Representation of architecture — 12 CFU (ICAR/06 Topography and cartography; ICAR/17 Drawing)
  • Architectural and urban design — 24 CFU/ECTS (ICAR/14 Architectural and urban design)
  • Theories and techniques for architectural restoration — 4 CFU (ICAR/19 Restoration)
  • Structural analysis and design for architecture — 8 CFU (ICAR/07 Geotechnics; ICAR/08 Solid and structural mechanics; ICAR/09 Structural engineering)
  • Urban design and territorial planning — 12 CFU/ECTS (ICAR/20 Urban planning and techniques; ICAR/21 Urban planning)
  • Technological disciplines for architecture and building production — 12 CFU (ICAR/10 Technical architecture; ICAR/11 Building production; ICAR/12 Architectural technology)
  • Evaluation disciplines for architecture and urban planning — 4 CFU (ICAR/22 Evaluation)
  Total: 108 CFU of prescribed curricular content.
(3) ENGLISH: possession of a level of knowledge of English not lower than B2 CEFR (see language_requirements).
(4) ITALIAN: 'a minimum level of knowledge of the Italian language'; if the level is judged insufficient during the interview, the student is directed to include Italian-language learning activities in their study path rather than being rejected.
(5) FOR ITALIAN CITIZENS ONLY: having passed the mandatory national admission test for enrolment in a bachelor's and/or single-cycle master's degree course expressly aimed at 'training as an architect'. This is a retrospective requirement referring to the test already sat at the undergraduate stage — it is NOT a new test to be taken for ARCHER, and by its own wording it does not apply to non-Italian citizens.
(6) PERSONAL PREPARATION: 'The adequacy of the student's personal preparation is verified upon entry through merit assessments of the degree score and the study plans followed in the three-year degree courses, as well as through interviews aimed at ascertaining the minimum and essential basic knowledge for the successful completion of the training course.'
(7) CURRICULAR SUPPLEMENTS: 'Any curricular additions must be completed before enrollment within the terms set out in the didactic regulations of the Degree Program.' A candidate cannot enrol while lacking the curricular requirements; missing credits are acquired by enrolling in single courses ('corsi singoli', 180 EUR per registration at Federico II). The university-wide FAQ for open-access two-year master's courses is explicit: 'Posso immatricolarmi se non possiedo i requisiti di accesso? No.' — and if a student enrols anyway, the Segreteria Studenti starts the procedure to annul the enrolment.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH (mandatory, hard requirement): a level of knowledge of English not lower than B2 of the CEFR. This is stated identically on the orientamento page, on the ARCHER application-rules page and in Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulations. Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations specifies the method of proof: 'Possession of a level of knowledge of the English language not lower than B2 of the CEFR, necessary for admission to the Degree Course, is verified through certifications from institutions legally recognized by the MUR pursuant the Ministerial Decree 9/2/2021 or subsequent regulations.' Non-EU applicants must upload a 'CEFR minimum level B2 English certification' as part of their pre-admission dossier. No specific numeric thresholds (e.g. an IELTS band or TOEFL score) and no list of named providers are published on the programme's own pages — the reference is generic to MUR-recognised certifying bodies under D.M. 9/2/2021, which in practice covers Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL, Trinity, Pearson and the other accredited providers. No provision for a university-run English placement test in lieu of a certificate is published, and no explicit exemption is published for applicants whose previous degree was taught in English.
ITALIAN (soft requirement, unusual for an English-taught degree): 'a minimum level of knowledge of the Italian language' is listed among the entry requirements. No CEFR level or certificate is specified. The Didactic Regulations state that the level is assessed 'during an interview' and that, where insufficient, 'students are directed to include in their didactic path's activities aimed at learning and strengthening their knowledge of the Italian language'. The study plan supports this: the 'Ulteriori attività formative' slot explicitly covers 'specific attention to the Italian language for foreign students', with a pass ('idoneità') awarded on presentation of a detailed report on the language work done, and the orientamento page notes that tutoring activities encourage international students to reach an acceptable level of Italian with the support of the University Language Centre (CLA). Separately, the University's international admission-regulation page confirms that for a degree course delivered in ENGLISH 'level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required' for the Universitaly pre-enrolment / visa stage, and that an international English certificate 'is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation'. So: B2 English is a genuine gate; Italian is a soft, remediable requirement checked at interview and never a B2 threshold.

The ARCHER page warns: 'Please note that you will be probably contacted for an interview before getting a pre-admission letter.' After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only.'). Because ARCHER is an OPEN-access (not restricted-access) programme, the post-15-June extension explicitly does NOT apply to it.  • Visa application at Italian Embassies/Consulates: by 2026-11-30 ('NOVEMBER – 30 – 2026 – Deadline for submitting the Visa Application at Italian Embassies /Consulates').

required_documents:
A. PRE-ADMISSION DOSSIER — non-EU citizens resident abroad (ARCHER 'Application rules' page): CV; passport; Bachelor's degree in Architecture; transcripts of courses and exams; CEFR minimum level B2 English certification; a letter of recommendation from a teacher expressly addressed to the ARCHER course (subject to verification); a letter of motivation; and a portfolio no longer than 20 pages 'with clear reference to design activities that concerned built heritage and landscape'. The 2024/25 ARCHER booklet gives infodiarcarcher@unina.it as the address to send the same dossier to. An interview normally follows, then the department issues a pre-admission letter.
B. UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT — non-EU citizens resident abroad: the online pre-enrolment application on https://www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri indicating University of Naples Federico II, the ARCHER programme and the chosen Embassy/Consulate, submitted TOGETHER WITH the pre-admission letter.
C. FOR THE VISA (international.unina.it): the summary of the pre-enrolment application validated by Federico II; any language competence certificates; a health insurance policy where applicable; and the documents for a foreign qualification. Visa financial requirement: proof of means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year, funds for repatriation, suitable accommodation and adequate medical insurance.
D. QUALIFICATION-RECOGNITION DOCUMENTS (both EU and non-EU routes): translations; legalisations; Diploma Supplement; certificates of examinations; a statement of comparability from the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre CIMEA (https://www.cimea.it/EN/); and/or a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the competent Italian diplomatic representation.
E. ENROLMENT (non-EU students): copy of passport; application form; 1 passport photo; Italian tax code (codice fiscale); proof of having applied for the residence permit; Declaration of Value or ENIC-NARIC/CIMEA certificate of validity.
F. ENROLMENT PACKAGE FOR OPEN-ACCESS TWO-YEAR MASTER'S COURSES (university FAQ 'CORSI DI LAUREA MAGISTRALE BIENNALE AD ACCESSO LIBERO'), to be delivered to the Segreteria Studenti counters within 10 days of receiving the matricola: the printed 'plico' (summary of the data entered in the Segrepass enrolment procedure); one passport-format photo (unless already uploaded online); a photocopy of a valid identity document; and — if the degree was obtained at a university other than Federico II — a self-certification of the degree under D.P.R. 445/2000 stating the awarding university, the exact title obtained, the date and mark of award, and the full list of examinations passed with, for each exam, the date, mark, number of CFU and SSD (disciplinary sector). That SSD-level exam list is what the Segreteria uses to check the ARCHER curricular credit table.
G. FEE DETERMINATION: an ISEEU (university ISEE) declaration must be available in the INPS database at the time of the first instalment, otherwise the maximum fee band applies. Students of foreign citizenship pay according to citizenship band instead (see tuition_or_fees_link).
H. PRACTICAL WARNING: the ARCHER application-rules page routes applicants to an 'APPLICATION' link that currently points to a Google Forms EDIT url (docs.google.com/forms/d/1mffpUj5zUMIPvj_xteBcgXIaKkiWb6G-baYyOad6VNs/edit), which ordinary applicants cannot open, and it spells the portal as 'www.universitaly.com' rather than the correct www.universitaly.it. Applicants should email the department (infodiarcarcher@unina.it / infodiarc@unina.it) or the coordinator directly.
entry_exam_or_test:
NO written entrance examination, NO TOLC, NO SAT and NO national admission test are required for this programme. The course is open access ('accesso libero') and Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations states plainly that 'The Degree Program does not include local access programming'. Federico II's 2026/27 restricted-access competition for architect-training courses (D.R. 2379 of 18/06/2026) covers only the single-cycle LM-4 Architettura, the single-cycle LM-4 Ingegneria edile-architettura and the L-17 Scienze dell'Architettura — the two-year LM-4 ARCHER is deliberately excluded, so there is no admission test to sit and no ranking to place in.
WHAT IS ASSESSED INSTEAD:
 • Curricular-requirement check: the Segreteria/CCD verifies the SSD-by-SSD credit table against the applicant's transcript.
 • Verification of personal preparation (compulsory for every candidate, and only accessible to those who already meet the curricular requirements): 'merit assessments of the degree score and the study plans followed in the three-year degree courses, as well as through interviews aimed at ascertaining the minimum and essential basic knowledge for the successful completion of the training course envisaged by the Degree Course'. So an INTERVIEW is a formally foreseen instrument.
 • For non-EU applicants resident abroad the interview is described more concretely on the application-rules page: 'Please note that you will be probably contacted for an interview before getting a pre-admission letter.' The same stage assesses a PORTFOLIO (max 20 pages, focused on design work on built heritage and landscape), a letter of motivation and a letter of recommendation — i.e. a portfolio-and-interview review rather than a standardised test.
 • The interview is also where the 'minimum level of knowledge of the Italian language' is judged.
 • English B2 is proven by certificate (MUR-recognised bodies under D.M. 9/2/2021), not by a test sat at the university.
 • RETROSPECTIVE TEST REQUIREMENT (Italian citizens only): applicants of Italian citizenship must have already passed the mandatory national admission test for an architect-training bachelor or single-cycle course. This is evidence of a test passed years earlier at undergraduate entry; it is not an exam taken for ARCHER, and the requirement is worded to apply only to Italian citizens.
seats_total: No fixed seat number is published — the programme is open access with no numerical cap. Art. 5 of the 2025/26 Didactic Regulations states 'The Degree Program does not include local access programming' ('Il corso non prevede programmazione locale degli accessi'), and orientamento.unina.it records the admission mode as 'Libero'. The programme is also absent from Federico II's 2026/27 national architect-training competition decree (D.R. 2379 of 18/06/2026), which is where seat numbers for the architecture area are set — that decree caps only the single-cycle LM-4 Architettura at 250+3 seats, the single-cycle LM-4 Ingegneria edile-architettura at 90+2, and the L-17 Scienze dell'Architettura at 176+4. None of those figures applies to ARCHER. Admission is therefore limited only by whether the individual candidate satisfies the curricular requirements, the B2 English requirement and the personal-preparation check — not by competition against other candidates for a limited number of places.
non_eu_reserved_seats: [uncertain] No reserved quota for non-EU citizens resident abroad is published for this programme on any unina.it, orientamento.unina.it, international.unina.it, corsi.unina.it or diarc.archer.unina.it page. This is consistent with the programme being open access: Federico II publishes numeric non-EU quotas only for its restricted-access ('numero programmato') courses. For reference, in the architecture area the 2026/27 architect competition decree D.R. 2379/2026 reserves 3 seats for non-EU citizens resident abroad on the single-cycle LM-4 Architettura, 2 seats (of which 1 for Chinese citizens under the 'Marco Polo' programme) on the single-cycle LM-4 Ingegneria edile-architettura, and 4 seats on the L-17 Scienze dell'Architettura — but ARCHER is not covered by that decree and none of those numbers applies to it. What non-EU applicants face instead is a qualitative gate (dossier + portfolio + interview + pre-admission letter) rather than a numeric quota. Italian universities do declare a non-EU 'contingente' per course on the Universitaly portal each year, but Federico II does not publish that figure for ARCHER on its own websites, so the exact number (if any) could not be verified from official unina.it sources and should be confirmed directly with infodiarcarcher@unina.it or segrearch@unina.it.
tuition_or_fees_link:
[uncertain — two official 2026/27 versions of the student fee guide give different regional-tax bands]
Main pages: https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/tasse-e-simulatore (Taxes and simulator, EN) and https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (Iscrizioni e tasse, IT). Fee simulator: http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ . Official 2026/27 fee guide: 'Guida rapida studente a.a. 2026/27' — https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 (the version linked from the unina.it news item, dated 10 July 2026) and https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_rapida_studente_2026-27-pdf-1 (the version linked from orientamento.unina.it). FAQ for this exact course category: https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/cdl_magistrale_biennale_accesso_libero-pdf ('Corsi di laurea magistrale biennale ad accesso libero').
SUMMARY FOR 2026/27: the tuition contribution is ISEEU-income-based and identical across all subject areas ('non sussiste alcuna differenza rispetto all'area di appartenenza del corso'). First-year students pay the 'contributo agevolato': fully exempt up to ISEEU 30,000 EUR; above that a fixed 1,011.50 EUR plus a variable component, rising to a maximum of 2,384.00 EUR for those who file no ISEEU declaration. A 50% reduction applies to students enrolling in the first year of a two-year master's who obtained their bachelor's degree by the month of October. On top of the contribution: the Campania regional right-to-study tax plus 16.00 EUR stamp duty.
REGIONAL TAX — CONFLICTING OFFICIAL FIGURES: the 10-July-2026 guide (linked from unina.it) gives three bands of 130.00 / 151.00 / 173.00 EUR (130 EUR for ISEEU up to 25,500 EUR and for students from particularly poor countries under art. 13 c.5 DPCM 9 April 2001 per D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026; 151 EUR for ISEEU 25,500.01–51,000 EUR AND for students whose household resides abroad; 173 EUR for ISEEU above 51,000 EUR or no ISEEU). The other 2026/27 guide version (linked from orientamento.unina.it) gives 125.50 / 146.50 / 167.50 EUR. The 130/151/173 set is the one carried by the unina.it-linked, explicitly dated version and by the D.M. 176/2026 reference, and is treated here as current.
CRITICAL FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: non-EU citizens ('stranieri — cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE') are FULLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus the 16 EUR stamp duty, by the ordinary first-instalment deadline. Citizens of other EU countries pay a flat fixed contribution of 200 EUR for enrolment (where the amount otherwise due would be 200 EUR or more). Foreign students who file no ISEEU pay the top band of the regional tax. The simplified figures on international.unina.it ('European students EUR 200/year tuition + EUR 140/year regional tax + EUR 16.00 legal stamp' and 'Non-european students EUR 140/year regional fee + EUR 16.00 legal stamp') are a stale summary — the 140 EUR regional-tax figure is from an earlier year.
INSTALMENTS 2026/27: 60% of the contribution + regional tax + stamp duty from 2026-07-16 (first-year master's enrolments) and by 2026-11-02; 20% by 2027-03-01; 20% by 2027-04-30. Late-enrolment surcharge +50 EUR to 2027-01-15 and +110 EUR from 2027-01-16; a further 100 EUR surcharge from 2027-07-16 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments.
OTHER RELEVANT CHARGES: enrolment in a single course ('corso singolo') costs 180 EUR — directly relevant to ARCHER applicants who must make up missing curricular credits or who use 'contract enrollment' to enrol late; duplicate parchment 52 EUR; transfer in/out 96 EUR; career suspension 202 EUR. There is NO separate international or English-track tuition for ARCHER — it uses the standard Federico II ISEEU system.

uncertainty_notes:
1) ADMISSION TYPE — RESOLVED WITH HIGH CONFIDENCE. The natural worry with an LM-4 programme is that it might fall under the national restricted-access regime for 'corsi finalizzati alla formazione di Architetto' (Law 264/1999). It does not. Three independent official sources agree: orientamento.unina.it records 'Admission: Libero'; Art. 5 of the 2025/26 Didactic Regulations states the course 'does not include local access programming'; and Federico II's own 2026/27 architect competition decree (D.R. 2379 of 18/06/2026) enumerates in Art. 1 only the single-cycle LM-4 Architettura, the single-cycle LM-4 Ingegneria edile-architettura and the L-17 Scienze dell'Architettura. The national test requirement appears in ARCHER's rules only retrospectively and only for Italian citizens, i.e. as proof that the applicant already passed the architecture entrance test when entering their bachelor. Note that international.unina.it's generic sentence 'Registration for admission tests for the Master of Science degree courses in Medicine and Surgery... and for courses aimed at training as an Architect, is carried out according to the procedures active on the portal' refers to those three restricted courses, not to ARCHER.
2) NON-EU APPLICATION DEADLINE CONFLICT. The programme page sets 2026-05-31 for the Universitaly submission; international.unina.it sets the university-wide pre-enrolment deadline at 2026-06-15 and extends it beyond that date only for RESTRICTED-access programmes — which ARCHER is not. The safe reading is that 2026-05-31 binds for ARCHER. Marked [uncertain] in application_deadline_non_eu. The 2024/25 booklet additionally contradicts itself internally (15 June vs 15 July 2024), which shows the department is not always precise about this date; applicants should confirm by email.
3) BOTH 2026/27 INTERNATIONAL DEADLINES HAVE ALREADY PASSED at the 2026-08-30 capture date (31 May and 15 June 2026). No a.y. 2027/28 dates were published on any unina.it page at capture time. Any 2027/28 figure would be an inference, and none is asserted here as fact.
4) EU/GENERAL ENROLMENT DEADLINE CONFLICT. unina.it says the Segrepass enrolment window runs 16 July – 2 November 2026; orientamento.unina.it says 16 July – 31 October 2026. Separately, the programme's own first-enrolment deadline is 31 December 2026 and the fee guide permits master's first-year enrolment up to 31 March 2027 — so three different 'deadlines' coexist, each governing a different thing (the standard fee-instalment window, the programme's own cut-off, and the statutory outer limit). Marked [uncertain] in application_deadline_eu.
5) LATE-ENROLMENT CFU THRESHOLD CONFLICT. orientamento.unina.it says 10 CFU; the ARCHER application-rules page says 8 CFU; the 2026/27 university guide sets a 6–12 CFU band within which each CCD chooses. The programme page's 8 CFU is the most specific and is used here.
6) REGIONAL TAX FIGURE CONFLICT. Two 2026/27 versions of the 'Guida rapida studente' are simultaneously online with different regional-tax bands (130/151/173 EUR vs 125.50/146.50/167.50 EUR). The 130/151/173 version is dated 10 July 2026, is linked from the unina.it news item, and cites D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026, so it is treated as current. Marked [uncertain] in tuition_or_fees_link. Note also that the summary figures on international.unina.it (200 EUR / 140 EUR) are stale.
7) NON-EU RESERVED SEATS NOT PUBLISHED. No non-EU quota for ARCHER appears anywhere on unina.it. This is expected for an open-access course, but it could not be positively confirmed that the quota is unlimited, because Italian universities do declare a per-course non-EU 'contingente' on Universitaly that Federico II does not mirror on its own sites. Marked [uncertain].
8) COURSE CODE / ACTIVATION YEAR. corsi.unina.it/DB2 gives 'Activation year 2020', while the course code changed from P53 to DB2 with the 2025/26 re-accreditation into class 'LM-4 R'. Both facts are consistent — the course has run since 2020 and was re-coded in 2025/26 — but a reader comparing the two class labels (LM-4 vs LM-4 R) may think they are different courses. They are not.
9) THE ITALIAN-LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT IS THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS BARRIER. Unlike most fully English-taught Italian master's programmes, ARCHER lists 'a minimum level of knowledge of the Italian language' among its formal entry requirements. It is not a B2 gate, has no named certificate, is assessed at interview and is remediable through study-plan activities — but it is a formal requirement and applicants with zero Italian should raise it with the coordinator in advance.
10) BROKEN APPLICATION LINK. The ARCHER application-rules page's 'APPLICATION' hyperlink points to a Google Forms EDIT URL (docs.google.com/forms/d/.../edit) that applicants cannot open, and the page misspells the portal as 'www.universitaly.com' (correct: www.universitaly.it). This is a live defect on the official page as of 2026-08-30 and means applicants realistically have to email infodiarcarcher@unina.it or the coordinator directly. It also implies the application-rules page may not be tightly maintained, which is a further reason to verify the dates directly.
11) NO DEDICATED PROGRAMME FEE STRUCTURE. ARCHER charges no separate international/English-track tuition — it uses Federico II's standard ISEEU system, under which non-EU citizens are fully exempt from the tuition contribution. This makes the effective annual cost for a non-EU student roughly 146–189 EUR (regional tax + stamp duty), which is unusually low and worth double-checking against the Segreteria before relying on it.
12) All data captured on 2026-08-30 exclusively from unina.it-family sources: orientamento.unina.it, corsi.unina.it, www.unina.it (including PDF decrees and guides), international.unina.it and diarc.archer.unina.it. No third-party aggregator was used for any factual field.
